caption_verbatim: Three-dimensional computed tomography scan of the craniovertebral junction and upper cervical spine in a 7-year-old with significant rotational abnormality of the occipitoatlantoaxial joints. Note the perching of the occiput on the right lateral atlantal mass of C1 and rotational luxation of C1 on C2. The patient, who had undergone tonsil and adenoid resection a few days prior, had Grisel syndrome.

caption_verbatim: Craniocervical instability in a 5-year-old with Down syndrome. (A) Lateral cervical radiograph shows atlantoaxial instability with pathologic atlantodental interval (10 mm, black line). (B) Three-dimensional computed tomography composite of skull base viewed from within shows anterior displacement of C1 with canal stenosis (arrowhead). Magnetic resonance (MR) images of the cervical spine show severe stenosis and cord signal change at the cervicomedullary junction due to anterior compression from atlantoaxial dislocation and posterior compression from the displaced bifid C1 posterior arch, evident on sagittal (C) and axial (D) views. (E) Operative view following C1 laminectomy with dorsal occiput–C2 fusion with customized contoured loop instrumentation. (F and G) Follow-up MR images (dynamic views) showing stable alignment.

caption_verbatim: Spastic quadriparesis with dysphagia, hoarseness, and sleep apnea in a 28-year-old despite prior transoral odontoidectomy and C1–C2 dorsal arthrodesis. (A) Midsagittal T2-weighted magnetic resonance image of craniocervical junction shows ventral compression at cervicomedullary junction from a ventral bony mass extending from the clivus with resultant cord signal change and myelomalacia. Composites of three-dimensional computed tomography visualizations of the craniocervical junction in midline section (B) and of the view from within the foramen magnum (C) indicate that the odontoid process apex has never formed, since the proatlas component of the odontoid is still unsegmented from the midline clivus (arrow).

caption_verbatim: Lower cranial nerve palsy and hemianesthesia in a 29-year-old. Complete atlas assimilation and abnormal odontoid-clivus angulation are evident on sagittal (A), coronal (B), and three-dimensional computed tomography (C) scans. Preoperative sagittal magnetic resonance images show tonsillar ectopia with ventral medullary indentation (D) and holocord syringohydromyelia (E). (F) Postoperative resolution of syrinx and restoration of cervicomedullary alignment following transoral odontoidectomy and dorsal occiput–C2 fusion.

caption_verbatim: A 14-year-old presented with progressive dysphagia and shortness of breath. Sagittal computed tomography (A) and magnetic resonance imaging (B) sequences indicate a proatlas segmentation abnormality with a horizontal clivus, atlas assimilation, and a shallow posterior fossa resulting in ventral medullary compression, tonsillar ectopia, and syringomyelobulbia (B). (C) The patient experienced neurological recovery after ventral craniovertebral junction decompression and dorsal occiput–C2 fusion.

caption_verbatim: A 13-year-old girl presented severely quadriparetic after a minor fall. Craniovertebral junction pluridirectional computed tomography scans in the frontal plane (A) and midline sagittal plane (B) indicate a dystopic os odontoideum. The ossicle has smooth, rounded cortical borders and is separated by a gap from a small hypoplastic dens. It is attached to the clivus. (C) Lateral radiograph of the same patient at 4 years of age following a rear-end motor vehicle accident. Note the atlantoaxial dislocation. She was treated with Minerva cast immobilization.

caption_verbatim: An 8-year-old child presented with severe neck pain. He had a history of a motor vehicle accident 3 to 4 years prior to presentation. Dynamic cervical radiographs indicated increased atlantodental interval in flexion (A, black line) that reduced with extension (B). (C) Sagittal magnetic resonance imaging sequence in neutral position shows abnormal atlantoaxial articulation. Computed tomography scans in three-dimensional visualization (D) and in sagittal view (E) indicate a dystopic os odontoideum. (F) The patient underwent C1–C2 screw fixation with rib supplementation. (G) Follow-up imaging shows stable atlantoaxial alignment.

caption_verbatim: A 10-year-old child presented with headaches, ataxia, spastic quadriparesis, and an unidentified bone-softening disorder. (A) Sagittal magnetic resonance image shows severe cervicomedullary compression and cervical spine syrinx. Sagittal (B) and coronal (C) two-dimensional computed tomography (CT) scans show markedly abnormal skull base with shallow-shaped posterior fossa and left-sided C1-occiput assimilation. (D) Axial CT scan shows anterolateral left-sided compression of spinal canal from C1 articular pillar (arrow). Three-dimensional CT visualizations from within the foramen magnum (E) and in a posterior view (F) indicate the pathologic occiput-C1 articulation (black arrows). (G) Lateral radiograph following foramen magnum and anterolateral C1 decompression with rib allograft fusion. Note the pathologic vermian bone formation within the sutures.
